faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subheading: Everything you need to know about installing and operating Assistant CLI.

items.question: What exactly does the installation script do on my system?
items.answer: The interactive installer clones the repository into ~/.config/assistant-cli (on Linux/macOS) or %LOCALAPPDATA%\assistant-cli (on Windows), detects your shell (Bash, Zsh, Fish, or PowerShell), and adds the init.sh loader to your terminal profile (~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, config.fish, or $PROFILE). Everything is done in user space without requiring root or administrator privileges.

items.question: Which AI engines are natively supported?
items.answer: Assistant CLI includes native support for Antigravity, GitHub Copilot, Ollama, OpenAI Codex, and OpenCode. Additionally, you can integrate any other provider or model by creating a .sh script inside custom/engines/.

items.question: How does Assistant CLI work on Windows via PowerShell?
items.answer: On Windows, the PowerShell installer creates a transparent wrapper function in your profile ($PROFILE) that invokes bash (via Git Bash) behind the scenes. This lets you run the "assistant" command directly in PowerShell or Windows Terminal with full support for arguments, colors, and interactivity without opening Git Bash manually.

items.question: What are built-in Skills and how do I create new ones?
items.answer: Skills are specialized modules with prompts and workflows designed for specific tasks: "assistant commit" analyzes git diff and generates semantic commits; "assistant resume" maps project trees and manifest files to summarize architecture; "assistant readme" generates comprehensive documentation in the selected language. You can easily create new skills with "assistant create skill <name> <file.md>".

items.question: How do configuration persistence and model switching work?
items.answer: All preferences (active engine, selected model for each engine, interface language, and release channel) are saved in data/config.txt. Each engine retains its own configured model in memory, allowing you to freely switch between providers without losing prior settings.

items.question: How do I update the assistant or switch between stable and beta channels?
items.answer: To update to the latest version of your current channel, run "assistant update". To pin or test a specific version, use "assistant update @{{version}}". To switch between development and stable versions, run "assistant channel beta" or "assistant channel stable".

overview.heading: What is Assistant CLI?
overview.description: Assistant CLI is a modular, ultralightweight, localized terminal wrapper written in Bash, designed to orchestrate local and cloud-based Large Language Models (LLMs) directly from the command line.

multiEngine.title: Native Multi-Engine
multiEngine.description: Switch between Antigravity, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Ollama, OpenCode, and custom drivers.

persistence.title: Persistence
persistence.description: Each engine retains its own preferred model. Switching engines never erases your previous choices.

skills.title: Built-in Skills
skills.description: Generate structured semantic commits, project technical resumes, and comprehensive READMEs.

extensible.title: Fully Extensible
extensible.description: Add new Markdown prompts, shell AI drivers, custom languages, and commands in the custom/ folder.

installation.heading: Installation Guide
installation.description: Assistant CLI features streamlined installers for Linux, macOS, and Windows (with PowerShell wrapper support).

quickStart.heading: Getting Started with Assistant CLI
quickStart.description: After installation, open a new terminal window or reload your profile. Verify that the command is working:
quickStart.code:
# 1. Check installed version
assistant --version

# 2. Inspect overall status
assistant status

interactionModes.heading: Interaction Modes: REPL vs One-Shot
interactionModes.description: Assistant CLI seamlessly adapts to rapid one-off workflows or deep interactive sessions.

repl.title: Interactive Mode (Chat REPL)
repl.description: Starts an ongoing conversation session with the configured engine and model.

oneshot.title: Direct Question Mode (One-Shot)
oneshot.description: Sends a single prompt directly and prints the formatted response to the terminal.
oneshot.exampleCode: assistant "How to create a middleware in Next.js?"

engines.heading: Drivers & Multi-Engine Architecture
engines.description: Assistant CLI treats AI providers as decoupled modular drivers. Switch between high-capacity cloud models and 100% offline local models with a single command.
engines.code:
# Display active engine and corresponding model
assistant engine

# Open interactive menu listing installed and uninstalled engines
assistant engine --list

# Switch the active engine immediately
assistant engine ollama
assistant engine agy
assistant engine opencode

# Display active engine status
assistant engine status

models.heading: Model Management per Engine
models.description: Each engine maintains its own model selection saved independently. When you switch from ollama to agy and later back to ollama, your model preference is seamlessly restored.
models.code:
# Interactive menu to pick a model for the current engine
assistant model --list

# Set a specific model for the active engine
assistant model set gemma4:e2b
assistant model set opencode/big-pickle

# Display the currently configured model
assistant model status
models.configDesc: All preferences are saved in a clean key-value format inside data/config.txt:

thinkMode.heading: Think Mode for Reasoning Models (Ollama)
thinkMode.description: Deep reasoning models (such as DeepSeek R1, Qwen QwQ) often generate extensive chain-of-thought blocks (<think>...</think>). Assistant CLI gives you granular control over this output.
thinkMode.persistentCode:
# Enable thinking mode (--think)
assistant think on

# Disable thinking mode (--think=false)
assistant think off

# Hide thinking output from terminal (--hidethinking)
assistant think hide

# Clear forced flags (model default)
assistant think clear

# Display configured status
assistant think status
thinkMode.runtimeCode:
# Force deep reasoning
assistant --think "Solve this graph algorithm"

# Disable reasoning for fast replies
assistant --no-think "Generate a JSON with 3 test objects"

# Hide the reasoning block
assistant --hide-think "Explain the difference between mutex and semaphore"

commit.title: Semantic Commit Assistant (assistant commit)
commit.description: Analyzes Git staging (git status, git diff --cached, and git diff --stat) and suggests atomic, standardized commits following the Conventional Commits specification (feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor, test).
commit.calloutText: The assistant does not execute git commands automatically. It outputs exact git add and git commit -m "..." commands for you to review, approve, and execute in your terminal.
commit.code:
# Stage your intended files
git add src/components/Button.tsx

# Ask assistant to generate suggestions
assistant commit

resume.title: Technical Project Summary Generator (assistant resume)
resume.description: Scans directory trees and package manifests (package.json, Cargo.toml, pom.xml, go.mod, requirements.txt, etc.) and generates structured Markdown documentation inside ./projects-resumes/.
resume.code:
# Analyze current directory
assistant resume

# Analyze a specific project
assistant resume ../my-react-project

# Analyze multiple projects in parallel using sub-processes
assistant resume ./app ./api ./web

readme.title: Professional README Generator (assistant readme)
readme.description: Analyzes complete project architecture and creates a full README.md with shields.io badges, table of contents, setup instructions, dependency tables, and examples in your preferred language.
readme.code:
# Generate README in Brazilian Portuguese
assistant readme --lang pt-br --name README-PTBR

# Generate README in default English
assistant readme --lang en --name README

customization.heading: Full Extensibility in the custom/ Folder
customization.description: Assistant CLI features a plug-and-play architecture that lets you build drivers for new AI tools, new skills with custom personas, new interface languages, and terminal commands without altering core source code.
customization.treeCode:
custom/
├── engines/             # Shell drivers (.sh) for new AI tools or APIs
├── locales/             # Translation files (.sh) adding new languages
├── skills/              # Markdown files (*-assistant.md) with personas and prompts
└── init.sh              # Bash functions for dynamic commands (_cmd_<name>)

gitBashPath.question: On Windows, I get an error stating that the 'bash' command was not found
gitBashPath.p1: The native Assistant CLI PowerShell wrapper requires the Git Bash executable to be in your system PATH.
gitBashPath.p2: It is usually located in C:\Program Files\Git\bin or C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin. Add this path to your Windows Environment Variables in system settings.
